pass_b_english: The Lord says that the one once chosen by his hands will not be taken away, for the one from his hands is not removed, as he says, 'I will do, and who will turn it back?' He has made the calling of the nations, or, in other words, he has saved those who were being led astray, and now he asks, 'Who will change this, that is, change it to not be so?' For, as the Savior himself says, no one will snatch the ones saved by him from the hand of God (John 10:28-29).

My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me; I give them eternal life, and they will not perish, and no one will snatch them from my hand; my Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch them from the hand of my Father (John 10:27-29). The Lord God, who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel, says, 'I will send to Babylon for your sake, and I will stir up all the fugitives, and the Chaldeans will be bound in ships' (Isaiah 43:14).

Through the things recently said, a strong exhortation has been given to those called from the nations to knowledge of him, and it has been shown that he alone has knowledge of the beginning, middle, and end, and that there is no other who can save completely; he is all-powerful, a wonder-worker, and the natures of things obey his nods, with the elements of the world serving him, and whatever he wills is certainly accomplished, with nothing lying at his feet to hinder him.

The Israelites, having slipped into idolatry and disobedience, needed much guidance and stability of mind, as well as much light and exhortations and reminders; God, in his power and glory, makes known to them the future and reveals the disasters that will befall the Babylonians, showing that they will be taken captive, and through this, the Israelites will be convinced that the shameful things of all are proclaimed through them, as I said.

As the discussion turns to great matters, God necessarily shows the incomparable glory of his power, saying, 'Thus says the Lord God, who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel' (Isaiah 43:14); for God wants to remind them of the past, of the redemption from Egypt, when a great multitude of miracles testified to him …
